chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Aban, from Abu al-Abbas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is neither forgiveness nor retaliation for the women.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on women's right to forgiveness and retaliation in Islamic inheritance and blood money law?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic principle that women are excluded from the rights of 'afw' (forgiveness) and 'qisas' (retaliation) in homicide cases, a ruling derived from the Quranic verse 'and for you is retaliation in what is killed' (2:178), which Shia scholars interpret as referring specifically to men. This distinction highlights the classical Shia view that the right of blood vengeance is tied to the male lineage and guardianship, ensuring that the primary heirs (usually male) hold the decisive authority in retribution or compensation.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad Al Kufy, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad Al Nahdy, from Muhammad Bin Al Waleed, from Aban, from Abu Al Abbas, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘There is neither forgiveness nor retaliation for the women’.
